<div class="review-text">
Cut and dried from the same formula from the first entry of the series, this elaborates and expands on a lot of the characters and setting from the first book with a relatively self-contained threat-of-the-week plot. This book is still fun and entertaining, but it is worth keeping in mind that you can only recycle the same core appeal for so long before it starts to grow dull. I would recommend reading this and maybe a few more books in the series, but eventually jumping ship. And of course, this is definitely a book intended for a younger audience.
</div>
